page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU features a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AES cryptography. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is absent, though the instance is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64-32as_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU scores ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the average tier. For machine learning tasks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M LLM models, but performance degrades significantly on larger models, resulting in a bottom 10% ranking for text generation on 70B parameter models due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-32as_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of paying for unneeded compute cores. This profile is appropriate for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, enterprise resource planning applications, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
